title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Day 2
contentZh:
Day 2 of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is here at San Francisco’s Moscone West. Explore innovative startups and solution providers in the Expo Hall, discover emerging technologies through live startup pitches, and use AI-powered matchmaking to connect with a community of 10,000+ founders, investors, startup teams, and technology leaders.

Whether you’re looking for your next investment, discovering solutions for your business, or gathering ideas to take back to your team, there’s plenty to explore today.

Today’s focus spans AI, with speakers from Nvidia, Waabi, Flock Safety, and Ricursive Intelligence, alongside Benchmark’s full partnership. Conversations will cover robotics, AI hardware, public safety, and venture investment.

Still deciding whether to come? Get your pass and join us at 50% off the original walk-up rate. Make discovery and networking your focus with an Expo+ Pass, or choose an eligible conference pass to add stage sessions, interactive roundtables, and Q&A breakouts.

Image Credits:Slava Blazer Photography

Day 2 highlights

Registration: 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Badge pickup and in-person registration is in the Level 1 lobby. All times below are Pacific Time.

Expo Hall

Open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Level 2. Explore 300+ startups alongside tech partners and solution providers across the Expo Hall. See products in action, discover tools that could help your business grow, and speak directly with the teams behind them.

Meet potential customers and partners, scout investment opportunities, or compare solutions to the challenges your team is facing. Give yourself time to explore companies beyond your usual area of interest.

Image Credits:Eric Slomonson, The Photo Group

Pitch Showcase Stage

Catch today’s enterprise fast pitches to discover emerging startups and see how founders make their case. Whether you’re building a company, scouting investments, or working in a startup team, find inspiration in how others explain their products, demonstrate value, and capture attention.

Note the companies and approaches that stand out, take fresh ideas back to your team, and meet the founders afterward to explore potential opportunities.

Stage sessions

With an eligible conference pass, explore the ideas, business strategies, and technologies shaping the startup ecosystem. Check the full agenda for session times and the complete Day 2 lineup.

Disrupt Stage

Hear perspectives that could inform your next business decision, investment thesis, or product strategy. Today’s highlights include:

AI, Surveillance, and the Future of Public Safety: Garrett Langley, Flock Safety

What We Believe Now: Benchmark’s Jack Altman, Peter Fenton, Chetan Puttagunta, Everett Randle, and Eric Vishria

When AI Starts Designing Its Own Hardware: Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini, Ricursive Intelligence

Startup Battlefield 200

Startup Battlefield continues with health tech and life sciences, plus enterprise and security, as contenders pursue a place in the final and $100,000 in equity-free funding.

Discover companies to follow, see how teams respond to investor scrutiny, and gather ideas for presenting your own products or evaluating new opportunities.

Image Credits:Kimberly White / Getty Images

Builders Stage

Explore what it takes to fund and grow a startup. Founders can sharpen their plans, investors can compare perspectives on what makes a business fundable, and startup teams can better understand the priorities shaping their next stage of growth.

Consider what the discussion means for your business, portfolio, or team, and compare perspectives with other attendees afterward.

The Series A in 2027: Jahanvi Sardana, Index Ventures; Shailendra Singh, Peak XV; and Janelle Teng Wade, Bessemer Venture Partners

How to Win When You’re Not Building AI: Mark Crane, General Catalyst; Shan Shan, Baillie Gifford; and Chris Yu, ALSO

Build Mode Live: Building From Zero to One: Juliana Di Simone, Forela; Arul Nigam, Circuit Breaker Labs; and Courtney Young, MyoGene Bio

Revealing AI Disruptors 60: What Can AI Do Next?: Parag Agrawal, Parallel Web Systems; Shay Grinfeld, Greenfield Partners; Anand Kannappan, Patronus; Alberto Taiuti, Reactor

The Real Tokenmaxxing: How the Best AI Companies Navigate a Multi-Model World: Mo Jomaa, Capital G; Vipul Ved Prakash, Together AI; and Zuzanna Stamirowska, Pathway

Image Credits:Slava Blazer Photography / Flickr (opens in a new window)

Building the Next Generation of AI Giants: Jas Khaira, Blackstone N1

The Zero-to-1K Playbook: How to Get Your First 1,000 Customers Without a Marketing Budget: Crystal Huang, GV (Google Ventures); Grant Lee, Gamma; and Elia Wallen, Engine

So You’ve Got a Hit Product. How Does Your Company Do It Again?: Maddi Holman, Daring Ventures; Filip Kaliszan, Verkada; Tamar Yehoshua, Atlassian

Real World AI Stage

Discover how AI is moving into physical products and environments, with opportunities to explore practical applications, emerging markets, and the challenges of deployment. Plus, witness a live robot demonstration.

Building AI Systems When Failure Is Not an Option: Nathan Michael, Shield AI; Mikell Taylor, General Motors; and Raquel Urtasun, Waabi

Come, Meet Stretch. The Robot Built for Real Life, Not a Demo Reel: Aaron Edsinger, Hello Robot

Robots Are Waiting for Their ChatGPT Moment. Here Is What Is Standing in the Way: Les Karpas, Nvidia

Operating at the Edge: How AI Works When the Cloud Doesn’t: Ali Agha, FieldAI; Michelle Lee, Medra; and Aidan Madigan-Curtis, Eclipse Ventures

Launching AI’s Orbital Infrastructure: Devin Coldewey and Blake Bullock, The Aerospace Corporation; Jeff Thornburg, Portal Space Systems; Jonny Dyer, Muon Space

Humanoid Robots Have Arrived: Live and On Stage: Jonathan Hurst, Agility Robotics, and Digit, Humanoid Robot

From Prototype to Production: Can It Scale in Reality: Kevin Peterson, Bedrock Robotics; Adrian Macneil, Foxglove

The Race to General-Purpose Robots with Skild AI: When AI Meets the Physical World: Varun Jain, SE Ventures; Deepak Pathak, Skild AI

Can We Engineer Nature’s Comeback?: Ben Lamm, Colossal Biosciences

Why and How Every Company Will Build Its Own AI: Manos Koukoumidis, Oumi; Matt Burns, Insight Media Group

AI Stage

The Agent Security Problem Nobody Is Talking About: Gavriel Cohen, NanoCo; Ric Smith, Okta

Rewriting SaaS: Why AI Breaks the Old Business Model: Cathy Gao, Sapphire Ventures; Aaron Jacobson, NEA; and Barr Moses, Monte Carlo

Before You Let AI Do the Job, How Do You Know It Actually Can: Irene Solaiman, Hugging Face

The $63 Billion Case for Storagemaxxing Your AI Stack: Pinaki Mukherjee, Wasabi Technologies; Stephanie Walter, HyperFRAME Research; Kevin Cochrane, Vultr; Jake Lee, L2 Point Management

What Comes After the Chatbot: Alexander Embiricos, OpenAI

The GTM Engineer: How AI Created Tech’s Next Big Job Category: Kareem Amin, Clay

Model Behavior: How Top Startups Get Real Value From AI Adoption: Cat de Jong, Anthropic; Grant Lee, Gamma; Kareem Amin, Clay

Proxy, Host, Operator: Who Can Read Your Agent’s Prompts?: Richard Rizk, Blackbox AI

Securing the AI Enterprise: Why the Cloud Just Got a Lot More Complicated: Katie Moussouris, Luta Security; Wendy Nather, Cybersecurity Veteran; Rudy Mitra, AWS

The Enterprise Isn’t Broken. Your Assumptions About It Are: Arsalan Tavakoli-Shiraji, Databricks

Breakout sessions

Use the audience Q&A to explore a decision you’re facing, ask how an idea could apply to your business, or better understand the implications for companies you’re evaluating.

Building Then vs Now: Payal Kadakia, ClassPass; Dr. Rumman Chowdhury, Humane Intelligence; Cassie Kozyrkov, Kozyr; Holly Ransom, Emergent

Infrastructure at the Speed of Demand: Power and Freight Without the Wait: Kofi Asante, Bluecore Energy; Kevin Damoa, Glīd

Best Practices for Running a Successful Fundraise: From Preparation to Investor Engagement: Maggie Sin, Fidelity Private Shares; Bill Tai, HUT 8 Corp; Robin
